** Playtime’s over
------------------------------------------------------------
https://radiomilwaukee.org/discover-music/artist-interviews/2026-10-01/brewers-playoffs-2026-chances-schedule

Jeff Levering is everything you want in an announcer. Calls a great game. Ratchets up excitement in key moments. Always has a cribbage board at the ready (at least according to the photo above). And after nearly 10 years with the Brewers, he also has a unique perspective on the team we all hope will finally make that long playoff run we’ve been dreaming about.

Before the Crew’s first postseason game this Saturday, Levering sat down with Jon Adler to talk about what’s he’s seen throughout the year that should have all of Milwaukee feeling optimistic about the weeks ahead.
Go to the interview (https://radiomilwaukee.org/discover-music/artist-interviews/2026-10-01/brewers-playoffs-2026-chances-schedule)

https://www.mlb.com/brewers/ballpark/events/venues

Hopefully, the Brewers’ season will be immediately followed by a celebration or two. But holiday parties will be here before you know it, and our local baseball team has a present for the good boys and girls who get their venue shopping done early.

If you book your holiday party at American Family Field before Oct. 31, you and all of your guests will receive a voucher redeemable for one ticket to a 2027 Brewers home game. It’s a great bonus on top of the locations inside the stadium that are their own gift:

The full-service brewery and restaurant at J. Leinenkugel’s Barrel Yard. The elevated experience of the Northwestern Mutual Legends Club. The gameday feel of the Visitors’ Clubhouse. The full swing of  X-Golf and its state-of-the-art simulators. There’s a spot for your entire holiday crew, whether it’s 10 people or 200.
Learn more (https://www.mlb.com/brewers/ballpark/events/venues)

The Milwaukee Brewers (https://www.mlb.com/brewers) are proud supporters of Radio Milwaukee.


** Un-beet-able
------------------------------------------------------------
https://radiomilwaukee.org/concerts/2026-09-30/milwaukee-concerts-this-week

One place you’ll definitely find a party this Saturday is the block right outside Cactus Club in Bay View. Since 2016, that’s where the beloved Milwaukee venue has hosted Beet Street and its spirit of collaboration that pulls in local organizations, vendors, food, drink and, of course, music.

As the event celebrates its 10th birthday, we all get a heck of a goodie bag in the form of a lineup that’s topped by standout L.A. outfit Automatic and Zamrock legends W.I.T.C.H. That made Beet Street an easy choice for this week’s Milwaukee Concert Picks, which also features a rare Brew City performance from Beck and 18 more excellent shows.
Check out the picks (https://radiomilwaukee.org/concerts/2026-09-30/milwaukee-concerts-this-week)

Milwaukee Concert Picks are sponsored by Urban Ecology Center (https://www.urbanecologycenter.org/) .

http://www.mkefilm.org/series/mmff-2026


** Move your feet
------------------------------------------------------------
https://radiomilwaukee.org/events-festivals/2026-10-01/what-to-do-milwaukee-weekend

While there will be dancing at concerts across the area, you should be at the Peck Pavilion this Saturday if you want to see some real pros. They’ve been invited to town by Nõ Studios for its annual Dance Fest, which is among the more rhythmic options in the latest weekend guide from Milwaukee With Kids.

On what’s looking like a lovely couple of weather days, you could also enjoy the last few Oktoberfests of the year, start spooky season at a few familiar haunts or fall into one of many autumn activities.
See what’s in the guide (https://radiomilwaukee.org/events-festivals/2026-10-01/what-to-do-milwaukee-weekend)


** A new perspective
------------------------------------------------------------
https://radiomilwaukee.org/podcast/cinebuds/2026-09-30/milwaukee-muslim-film-festival-2026-schedule

If you want to see something from a different point of view, there are few better places to go than your local movie theater — particularly if it’s the Oriental Theatre this weekend. The East Side cinema is hosting the Milwaukee Muslim Film Festival now through Sunday, giving you the chance to dangle 900 feet above a ravine in the remote Himalayan foothills without leaving southeastern Wisconsin.

Hanging by a Wire is one of the more pulse-poundings selections in this year’s festival, which we explored on the latest episode of Cinebuds with some help from an event insider.
Check out the festival lineup (https://radiomilwaukee.org/podcast/cinebuds/2026-09-30/milwaukee-muslim-film-festival-2026-schedule)

Cinebuds is sponsored by Joe Wilde Garage Doors (https://www.joewilde.com/) .

https://milwaukeemerch.com/collections/radio-milwaukee


** A way forward
------------------------------------------------------------
https://radiomilwaukee.org/podcast/uniquely-milwaukee/2026-10-01/my-way-out-milwaukee

A less conventional approach to shifting perspective is virtual reality, which can be a fun way to play around but also a powerful tool with the right application. We found a great example at a class provided by My Way Out, a program that provides reentry services to justice-impacted individuals.

Uniquely Milwaukee host Kim Shine joined a recent session to see how attendees explored everything from construction to automotive tech — without getting their hands dirty.
Listen to the episode (https://radiomilwaukee.org/podcast/uniquely-milwaukee/2026-10-01/my-way-out-milwaukee)


** Art and soul
------------------------------------------------------------
https://radiomilwaukee.org/podcast/uniquely-milwaukee/2026-09-29/art-resale-shop-milwaukee

Our Uniquely Milwaukee team also popped over to West Allis this week and a new store that’s helping overcome a surprising hurdle to creativity: the cost of art supplies.

414 Art Revival co-owners Julianna Jackson and Nate Carpenter know that challenge well, but they also had firsthand knowledge of a solution thanks to the store run by Jackson’s mom in Illinois. So the pair literally set up shop in West Allis and, not long after they opened their doors in July, were wonderfully overwhelmed by the community response.
Go shopping with us (https://radiomilwaukee.org/podcast/uniquely-milwaukee/2026-09-29/art-resale-shop-milwaukee)


** Maximum ‘Effort’
------------------------------------------------------------
https://radiomilwaukee.org/local-music/2026-10-01/new-milwaukee-music-glitzy

There’s a not-so-fun overwhelmed feeling that happens in just about every relationship as inevitable issues arise. The question is how we deal with those moments. Are we honest? Do we apologize? Do we disappear?

Local band Glitzy embarked on that choose your own adventure when they wrote “Effort” for upcoming album Say Sorry / You’re Right. The track alternates between gentle moments and heavier sounds, and we were thrilled to help them debut it as today’s Milwaukee Music Premiere.
Enjoy the song (https://radiomilwaukee.org/local-music/2026-10-01/new-milwaukee-music-glitzy)


** In the community
------------------------------------------------------------
https://radiomilwaukee.org/podcast/uniquely-milwaukee/2026-09-24/juan-miguel-martinez-county-supervisor

Juan Miguel Martinez is the kind of person you want representing your neighborhood. The Milwaukee County Supervisor for District 12 is just as likely to be at a podium talking about the park system as in a kitchen literally feeding his community (he’s on the left in the photo above).

Even with that busy schedule, Martinez found time to talk with Paula Lovo about his unlikely political career and how the doubts he felt initially turned into so much love from a movement he’s proud to be a part of.
Get to know Martinez (https://radiomilwaukee.org/podcast/uniquely-milwaukee/2026-09-24/juan-miguel-martinez-county-supervisor)
